interest: Nazi Party rosters of Germans in Japan from captured Berlin records, including Richard Sorge and Carl Juchheim.
overview: This file (894.00-N/7-1946 and 894.00-N/7-2446) consists of internal U.S. State Department memoranda and mimeographed rosters prepared in Berlin by the 6889th Berlin Documents Center under the Office of Military Government for Germany (US) concerning Nazi Party (NSDAP) members residing in Japan. Sent in July 1946 by Mr. Amshey of the Division of Foreign Activity Correlation to Mr. Lory of the Division of Japanese Affairs, the documentation comprises an initial roster dated June 18, 1946, followed by Supplementary List No. 1 dated June 25, 1946, both compiled from captured central NSDAP card indices in Germany. The lists systematically detail party membership numbers, dates of admission, dates and places of birth, Japanese residential addresses (predominantly in Tokyo, Yokohama, Kobe, and Hyogo Prefecture), and civilian occupations for German expatriates. These intelligence records were compiled and forwarded to the U.S. Political Adviser in Tokyo to support the identification, internment, and repatriation of German nationals and the de-Nazification of occupied Japan.

subfiles.summary: Issued on June 18, 1946, by the 6889th Berlin Documents Center under the Office of Military Government for Germany (US), this document provides an alphabetical register of German nationals in Japan who held membership in the NSDAP. For each individual, the list records their party membership number, date of joining, date and place of birth, last known address in Japan (mostly in Tokyo, Yokohama, and Kobe), and profession. Notable entries include German Embassy counsellor Erich Boltze, various diplomats, teachers, engineers, merchants, and renowned Soviet intelligence agent Richard Sorge.
